question: When barium chloride reacts with aluminium sulphate, it gives aluminium chloride along with:

options.text: a white colour precipitate of barium oxide
a white colour precipitate of barium sulphate
a yellow colour precipitate of barium sulphate
a white colour precipitate of barium chloride

solution:
The correct answer is __**a white colour precipitate of barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barium chloride (BaCl₂) reacts with aluminium sulphate [Al₂(SO₄)₃] to produce aluminium chloride (AlCl₃) and barium sulphate (BaSO₄).**
 
• **Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is formed as a precipitate, which is white in color.** This is due to its insolubility in water.
 
• The reaction can be represented as:

 **3BaCl₂ + Al₂(SO₄)₃ → 2AlCl₃ + 3BaSO₄↓**
 
• This is a typical example of a double displacement reaction, where the ions in the reactants exchange places to form new compounds.
 
• **The precipitate of barium sulphate is commonly used to confirm the presence of sulphate ions in qualitative analysis.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barium sulphate (BaSO₄):**

 
 
• **Properties:** It is a white crystalline solid and highly insoluble in water.
 
• **Uses:** It is used in medical imaging (barium meals) and as a filler in paints and plastics.
 
• **Occurrence:** Found naturally as the mineral barite.
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reactions:**
 
 
• These reactions involve the exchange of ions between two compounds to form new compounds.
 
• Example: Reaction between NaCl and AgNO₃ to form NaNO₃ and AgCl.
 
 
 
• **Qualitative analysis of sulphate ions:**
 
 
• Barium chloride is commonly used to test for sulphate ions in a solution.
 
• Presence of sulphate ions produces a white precipitate of barium sulphate.
 
 
 
• **Aluminium chloride (AlCl₃):**
 
 
• It is a hygroscopic compound and is often used as a catalyst in chemical reactions like Friedel-Crafts alkylation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Barium Sulphate Precipitate:**

 
 
• It is highly insoluble in water, which makes it an effective reagent for detecting sulphate ions.
 
• Its white color makes it easily visible during qualitative analysis.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Barium Compounds:**
 
 
• Barium compounds, such as barium sulphate and barium chloride, are widely used in laboratories and industries.
 
• Barium sulphate is used in X-ray imaging and paints, while barium chloride is used for water purification and the detection of ions.
 
 
 
• **Reactions Involving Aluminium:**
 
 
• Aluminium salts like aluminium chloride are highly reactive and are used in various chemical processes as catalysts.
 
• They are also used in the production of dyes and in water treatment plants.
